subject.title: Workspace symlinks to ~/.openclaw subdirectories are rejected by boundary path check

question: Should fixed workspace bootstrap files be allowed to resolve through symlink hops outside the workspace into selected `.openclaw` roots, and should that policy live in fs-safe or in an OpenClaw bootstrap wrapper?
rationale: The behavior is source-reproducible, but the fix changes which local filesystem roots can feed startup prompt authority, so automation should not choose the trust boundary alone.

options.title: Narrow Bootstrap Policy
options.body: Allow only fixed bootstrap-file symlink hops through the workspace bootstrap reader, with explicit denial of credentials, sessions, state, caches, logs, and direct arbitrary `.openclaw` reads.

options.title: Keep Current Rejection
options.body: Continue rejecting out-of-workspace symlink targets and improve diagnostics so users see why bootstrap files are missing.

options.title: Broader `.openclaw` Allowance
options.body: Allow any target under `.openclaw`, accepting higher prompt-injection and private-state exposure risk for sync ergonomics.

recommendation.title: Narrow Bootstrap Policy
recommendation.body: Allow only fixed bootstrap-file symlink hops through the workspace bootstrap reader, with explicit denial of credentials, sessions, state, caches, logs, and direct arbitrary `.openclaw` reads.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc has the current live maintainer comment and the overlapping open replacement PR, making them the best available owner for the policy choice.
